summary.title: Fixing failing calculator tests in calculator.py
summary.body:
I fixed the bug: `subtract` in `calculator.py:6` returned `a + b` instead of `a - b`, so `subtract(5, 3)` gave 8 instead of 2. With that changed, `python3 -m unittest` ran 4 tests, all passed, and it exited with code 0. I didn't touch the tests.

What the two diagnostics showed:
1. **`python3 -c "print('diag ' * 8000)"`:** the output was cut off at the bash tool's 30,000-character limit, so only about three-quarters of the ~40,000 characters came back.
2. **`sleep 5 && python3 -m unittest` with timeout 2000:** the command was killed at 2 seconds, while still in `sleep 5`. It returned no output, so the tests never ran in that call.

My first attempt at the edit was rejected because I hadn't opened the file with the Read tool yet. The test run right after it still failed for that reason. I read the file, made the edit, and the run above is the one that passed.
